subject: refrigerator in kitchen
title: What If You Never Had a Fridge?

scenes.text: What if you never had a fridge? Your leftovers would turn on you within hours.
Between 40 and 140 degrees Fahrenheit, bacteria on food can double in as little as twenty minutes.
That's why food safety experts say two hours out at most, and just one hour on a day above 90 degrees.
Without cold storage, you'd be back to salting, smoking and pickling everything, like people did before fridges.
A century ago, stomach cancer was America's top cancer killer. Refrigeration, and less salted food, helped bring it down.
The humming box in your kitchen is quietly protecting your stomach.

description:
What if you never had a fridge? USDA says bacteria can double in as little as 20 minutes in the Danger Zone of 40 to 140 degrees F, so perishable food shouldn't sit out more than 2 hours (1 hour above 90 degrees F).
The American Cancer Society notes stomach cancer was the leading cause of US cancer death in the early 1900s; refrigeration, which reduced salted and smoked foods, is one reason it declined.
